creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 7, item 1.

Since v0.12 quotes interpolations in shell commands, a command held in a string and run as `$`{cmd}`` becomes one quoted word. This was the correct spelling on v0.11 and now fails only when the branch runs:

```rad
cmd = "echo hi there"
$`{cmd}`
```

```
⚡️ 'echo hi there'
zsh:1: command not found: echo hi there
error[RAD20048]: Command exited with code 127
```

`rad check` reports no diagnostics, and the v0.12 migration guide does not mention this shape (it covers building a command as a string and running `$cmd`, the neighboring case). The fix in the script is `$cmd`.

A checker diagnostic for a command literal whose entire content is a single interpolation would be exact: no reading of that shape wants the quoting. The hint should point at `$cmd` and the migration guide should gain a line.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1).

Where: rts/check/ast_checks.go (new AST check on shell command literals).
title: Flag a shell command whose whole body is one interpolation
